1.1.1.open_ended_text: SPACE (Superb Prompt Automatic Creation Engine) is a programmable specification engine that transforms structured elicitation probes into development specifications. It sits at the intersection of prompt engineering, software specification, and developer tooling.

1.1.2.open_ended_text: The primary audience is software developers and technical leads building LLM-powered applications or complex systems who need structured specifications. They understand TypeScript/Node.js and are comfortable with JSON/YAML.
1.1.2.multi_choice_text: Experts / researchers — people who work in this domain daily

1.2.1.open_ended_text: Assumed: CLI tools, npm/Node.js, basic TypeScript, JSON/YAML, REST APIs. Must explain: 7-series elicitation methodology, dependency chains, artifact extraction, and how 326 probes produce a coherent spec.
1.2.1.multi_choice_text: Core fundamentals assumed; edge cases and advanced topics explained

1.2.2.open_ended_text: Mixed approach — architecture diagrams for the dependency graph, then concrete code examples from the TypeScript engine showing question flow through router, answer recording, artifact extraction, and export.
1.2.2.multi_choice_text: Mixed — conceptual frameworks illustrated with examples

1.3.1.open_ended_text: Standard software engineering terms (session, artifact, framework, series, round). SPACE-specific: probe (elicitation question), artifact (extracted data), series (themed rounds), round (batch of questions).
1.3.1.multi_choice_text: Standard industry terminology — use common terms precisely

1.3.2.open_ended_text: Progressive — start with simple question-asking, layer in dependencies, artifact accumulation, multi-format export, then intelligence layer. Each layer builds on previous.

2.1.1.open_ended_text: Core: Framework (326-probe set), Session (interaction instance), Project (session container), Artifact (extracted data), Series (themed rounds), Round (2 questions + follow-ups), Question (open-ended probe), Export (spec documents), User, Engine (orchestration).
2.1.1.multi_choice_text: 5–10 entities — moderate complexity with clear boundaries

2.1.2.open_ended_text: 3-5 attributes per entity. Framework: version, total_series, dependency_graph. Session: id, status, answers map, artifacts. Artifact: value, source_question_id, confidence. Series: id, name, depends_on, provides.
2.1.2.multi_choice_text: 3–5 attributes per entity — moderate descriptive richness

2.1.3.open_ended_text: Three categories: (1) Structural (Framework, Series, Round, Question) — probe taxonomy. (2) Runtime (Session, Engine, User) — execution. (3) Output (Artifact, Export) — derived data.

2.2.1.open_ended_text: Core: Framework, Session, Question, Artifact, Engine. Peripheral: Project (wrapper), User (implicit), Export (derived). System works with just core set; peripherals add organization and delivery.
2.2.1.multi_choice_text: Roughly equal split between core and peripheral entities

2.2.2.open_ended_text: Moderate — Questions fine-grained (326 unique), Rounds/Series moderate groupings, Artifacts fine-grained per-question but aggregate into dictionary. Balance keeps entity count manageable.
2.2.2.multi_choice_text: Moderate — key specializations become distinct entities

2.2.3.open_ended_text: Shared attributes by category. Runtime entities share lifecycle pattern. Structural entities share naming convention (dot-separated IDs). Artifacts share interface but content varies by source series.
2.2.3.multi_choice_text: Shared attributes grouped by category — entities in same category share a profile

2.3.1.open_ended_text: Tightly bounded — generates specs, does not implement/deploy them. Boundary: input = answers to 326 probes, output = structured spec documents.
2.3.1.multi_choice_text: Tightly bounded — scope is narrow and well-defined

2.3.2.open_ended_text: 3 actors: (1) Human user — provides domain knowledge. (2) LLM (optional) — auto-answer or refine. (3) File system — persists sessions. System works without external services.
2.3.2.multi_choice_text: 1–3 external actors (users, upstream data sources, downstream consumers)

2.3.3.open_ended_text: Stateful with versioned artifacts. Sessions: created → in_progress → completed. Questions: locked → available → answered. Supports snapshot/resume.
2.3.3.multi_choice_text: Stateful lifecycle — entities pass through defined states with transition rules

2.4.1.open_ended_text: No major gaps. One addition: "Configuration" entity for runtime settings (LLM provider, export formats). Currently embedded in Engine config.
2.4.1.multi_choice_text: No gaps — the current entity list is comprehensive

2.4.2.open_ended_text: No merges or splits needed. Boundaries are clean. "User" could split into Respondent/Consumer but adds complexity without benefit at current scale.
2.4.2.multi_choice_text: No changes needed — current classification is sound

2.4.3.open_ended_text: (1) Framework immutable after loading. (2) Answers append-only during session. (3) Artifacts derived, recomputed from answers. (4) Series dependencies strict.
2.4.3.multi_choice_text: Moderate constraints — several required fields and validity rules

2.5.1.open_ended_text: Edge cases: empty project, corrupted session JSON (validation on load), missing framework (fallback defaults), concurrent sessions (allowed but uncoordinated), long answers (>10KB accepted).
2.5.1.multi_choice_text: Known edge cases — they are well-understood and can be handled explicitly

2.5.2.open_ended_text: Hierarchical composition: Framework→Series→Round→Question. Sessions contain Answers and Artifacts. Projects contain Sessions. Dependency graph creates cross-series composition.
2.5.2.multi_choice_text: Containment — some entities serve as containers for others (1-level deep)

2.5.3.open_ended_text: Framework 1:N Series, Series 1:N Rounds (always 2 questions), Project 1:N Sessions, Session N:M Questions via answers, Session 1:N Artifacts, Series N:M via dependency graph.
2.5.3.multi_choice_text: One-to-many — common pattern with one parent referencing multiple children

3.1.1.open_ended_text: Framework CONTAINS Series, Series CONTAINS Rounds, Round CONTAINS Questions, Session ANSWERS Questions (many:many), Session EXTRACTS Artifacts, Project OWNS Sessions, Export FROM Session+Artifacts.
3.1.1.multi_choice_text: Moderate — roughly one association per entity on average

3.1.2.open_ended_text: Composition dominates — whole-part relationships. Exception: dependency graph between Series (DAG of artifact consumption). Answers map is association table linking Questions to responses.
3.1.2.multi_choice_text: 2–3 distinct relationship types (e.g., owns, produces, references)

3.2.1.open_ended_text: Hierarchical containment with flat dependency layer. Framework→Series→Round→Question is strict containment. Dependencies are flat (Series reference by ID). Artifacts float across hierarchy.
3.2.1.multi_choice_text: No hierarchy — all entities are peers with no containment structure

3.2.2.open_ended_text: Composition primarily — Artifacts composed into Session, not inherited. Exception: Export hierarchy shares interface (content+filename+mime_type) with different serialization strategies.
3.2.2.multi_choice_text: No inheritance — each entity is unique in its type

3.3.1.open_ended_text: Sequential causation with parallel-reads. Answering 1.1.1 enables downstream Series. Within Rounds, both Questions can be answered in any order. DAG — no cycles.
3.3.1.multi_choice_text: No causal links — entities change independently

3.3.2.open_ended_text: DAG with 7 nodes, ~10 edges. Critical path: S1→S2→S3→S4→S5→S6→S7. Branching where S5 depends on both S1 and S4.
3.3.2.multi_choice_text: Simple chain — a linear sequence of prerequisites

3.4.1.open_ended_text: Mostly immutable — answers append-only, editing allowed before completion. Artifacts recomputed from answers. Session status transitions one-way.
3.4.1.multi_choice_text: State-gated — relationships can only change when entities are in certain states

3.4.2.open_ended_text: Two junction entities: (1) Answers map — question_id to AnswerEntry with text, choice, timestamps. (2) Artifacts dictionary — artifact keys to ArtifactValue with provenance and confidence.
3.4.2.multi_choice_text: Transitive — some relationship types imply transitive chains

4.1.1.open_ended_text: Primary: elicitation session (create project → answer questions → extract artifacts → generate exports). Secondary: save/resume, artifact accumulation, progress tracking.
4.1.1.multi_choice_text: Narrow — a single well-defined task with clear boundaries

4.1.2.open_ended_text: 5 phases: (1) Init — create project, load framework. (2) Elicitation — 67 questions, 25 rounds. (3) Extraction — 66 artifacts via mapping. (4) Validation — contradictions, gaps. (5) Export — multi-format docs.
4.1.2.multi_choice_text: 5–8 steps — moderate complexity with clear waypoints

4.2.1.open_ended_text: 8-10 steps per question: router selects → display question → user answers → user classifies → validate → record → extract artifacts → check round → check series → advance.
4.2.1.multi_choice_text: Few branches — 1–2 decision points with 2–3 choices each

4.2.2.open_ended_text: 2-3 sub-actions per step. "Display" checks dependencies, formats context, shows progress. "Submit" validates text, records timestamp, updates map, recomputes artifacts, checks completion.
4.2.2.multi_choice_text: Simple I/O — each step takes one input and produces one output

4.3.1.open_ended_text: Three decision points: (1) Question routing — dependency graph + completion state. (2) Answer validation — non-empty, valid choice. (3) Completion detection — round/series/session.
4.3.1.multi_choice_text: Minimal — errors abort the procedure with a clear message

4.3.2.open_ended_text: Main: dependencies met → show question, else → skip. Secondary: valid → record, else → re-prompt. Tertiary: round complete → check series → check session → generate exports.
4.3.2.multi_choice_text: Fine — each step is a single atomic action

5.1.1.open_ended_text: TypeScript/Node.js for engine, CLI, storage. Python for web server. Single HTML+Tailwind for web UI. No external runtime dependencies beyond Node.js built-ins.

5.1.2.open_ended_text: Minimum: Node.js 18+, 512MB RAM, 100MB disk. Recommended: Node.js 20+, 2GB RAM, 1GB disk. ~3500 LOC TypeScript, 36KB HTML UI, ~10KB per session.

5.1.3.open_ended_text: Offline-first — zero network access for core. LLM integration optional (needs internet). Web UI served locally. No bandwidth/latency requirements.

5.1.4.open_ended_text: JSON files on local filesystem. SQLite adapter exists for future scaling but not integrated. No databases, object storage, or caching needed.
5.1.4.multi_choice_text: Single database — one relational or document store covers all needs

5.1.5.open_ended_text: Local development only. No cloud/on-premise/hybrid. Runs on developers machine. Web server binds to localhost. CLI installed via npm.
5.1.5.multi_choice_text: Cloud-native — designed for a specific cloud provider

5.2.1.open_ended_text: TypeScript for business logic. Python for web server. HTML+Tailwind via CDN for web UI. No frontend build step. Compiles to ES2022 JavaScript.
5.2.1.multi_choice_text: Two languages — e.g., backend + frontend split

5.2.2.open_ended_text: Cross-platform: macOS, Linux, Windows. Tested on Node.js 18/20/22. Platform-independent paths. Modern browsers for web UI.

5.2.3.open_ended_text: Runtime: commander, chalk, inquirer, ora, js-yaml, sql.js. Dev: vitest, tsx, typescript. Optional: openai, anthropic SDKs. No databases, message queues, external services.
5.2.3.multi_choice_text: Minimal dependencies — build from standard library where possible

5.2.4.open_ended_text: Semantic versioning (v2.1.0). Framework format versioned separately (v1→v2 migration built in). Backward compatible — old sessions load in new versions.
5.2.4.multi_choice_text: Latest-stable — always use current versions, update frequently

5.2.5.open_ended_text: npm for packages/distribution. tsc for build. Vitest for testing. No CI/CD yet — manual builds. prepublishOnly runs build+test. No Docker/K8s/cloud.
5.2.5.multi_choice_text: Simple build — single build tool, manual or script-based deployment

5.3.1.open_ended_text: Single-user interactive. Session: <100ms. Routing: <10ms. Submit: <50ms. Extract: <20ms. Export: <500ms. All under 1 second. No concurrency.
5.3.1.multi_choice_text: Low traffic — <100 req/s, seconds of latency, single-digit concurrency

5.3.2.open_ended_text: 326 questions, ~66 artifacts/session, ~10KB/session file. 5-10 sessions per project. ~500KB total per project. Designed for hundreds of projects.
5.3.2.multi_choice_text: Small — <10GB data, slow growth, single-node viable

5.3.3.open_ended_text: Not applicable — local dev tool. No SLA/uptime. Works offline. Completes in <1 second. Data durability via filesystem + optional git.
5.3.3.multi_choice_text: Best-effort — no formal SLA, occasional downtime acceptable

5.3.4.open_ended_text: Single-process, single-user. No horizontal scaling. Web server handles one request at a time. No load balancing/caching/CDN.
5.3.4.multi_choice_text: Vertical — scale up a single node as needed

5.3.5.open_ended_text: Standard dev tool practices. API keys in env vars. Local JSON files. No encryption/auth/audit logging needed for development tool.
5.3.5.multi_choice_text: Basic — password auth, TLS, no formal compliance requirements

5.4.1.open_ended_text: 5 LLM providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, Ollama. Unified LLMProvider interface. File system for storage. npm for distribution. Works without LLM (template provider).
5.4.1.multi_choice_text: 1–2 integrations — limited surface area for interoperability

5.4.2.open_ended_text: File system API for persistence. LLM providers use native REST APIs via SDK. Web server uses HTTP REST. No gRPC/WebSocket/message queues. All synchronous.

5.4.3.open_ended_text: Phase 1 (done): Engine+CLI. Phase 2: Web UI. Phase 3: LLM providers. Phase 4: Export. Phase 5: Persistence. Phase 6: Intelligence. Phase 7: npm publish. ~4 weeks development.

5.4.4.open_ended_text: TDD with 142 tests across 13 files. Phase-specific test files. Integration tests for session flows. Snapshot tests for exports. Manual web UI testing.
5.4.4.multi_choice_text: Standard — dev, staging, production with automated test suite

5.4.5.open_ended_text: npm package with README, LICENSE, TypeScript declarations. CLI help for every command. Inline JSDoc. Meta directory with specs/dev plans/audits. Self-documenting web UI.
5.4.5.multi_choice_text: Standard — API docs, architecture decision records, setup guide

6.1.1.open_ended_text: Iterative in 7 phases: Foundation → Engine → LLM → Export → UI → Persistence → Intelligence. Each phase independently testable. ~3500 LOC total.
6.1.1.multi_choice_text: Continuous flow (Kanban) — pull-based with WIP limits, no fixed iterations

6.1.2.open_ended_text: Solo developer — all roles (architecture, implementation, testing, docs). Small enough for full context. No coordination overhead. Fast decisions.
6.1.2.multi_choice_text: Solo or pair — 1–2 people, all roles combined

6.2.1.open_ended_text: TypeScript strict mode. 142 tests/13 files. Snapshot tests for exports. Integration tests for flows. No code review (solo). TypeScript catches type errors.
6.2.1.multi_choice_text: Standard — mandatory reviews, unit + integration tests, CI gates

6.2.2.open_ended_text: Boy scout rule — clean while building. Refactor when it helps new features. No dedicated refactoring phases. Main debt: web UI lacks tests, SQLite not integrated.
6.2.2.multi_choice_text: Opportunistic — clean as you go, no formal tracking

6.3.1.open_ended_text: Solo dev — self-documentation. Architecture in meta/specs/ markdown. Code is primary docs. TypeScript types self-describing. No meetings/formal comms.
6.3.1.multi_choice_text: Async-first — written docs, Slack/Teams, minimal meetings

6.3.2.open_ended_text: BDFL — one person decides. No RFC/ADR reviews. Decisions made quickly, documented after. Framework JSON is source of truth for question taxonomy.
6.3.2.multi_choice_text: BDFL — one person makes final decisions with input

7.1.1.open_ended_text: npm publish as space-cli. Global install via npm install -g. Web UI bundled but local — clone repo, run server. No separate distribution.
7.1.1.multi_choice_text: Automated CI/CD — merged to main triggers build + deploy pipeline

7.1.2.open_ended_text: npm for distribution, GitHub for source. No Docker — Node.js CLI runs anywhere. Web UI zero-dependency (single HTML + Python server). No cloud deployment.
7.1.2.multi_choice_text: Dev / staging / production — standard promotion pipeline

7.2.1.open_ended_text: Not applicable — dev tool, not production service. No logging/monitoring/alerting. Closest: session progress tracking and artifact quality scores.
7.2.1.multi_choice_text: Minimal — basic logging to stdout, manual check-ins

7.2.2.open_ended_text: Config via CLI flags and env vars. No feature flags/runtime config. Framework JSON is primary config. LLM settings are env vars. Minimal configuration by design.
7.2.2.multi_choice_text: Static config — environment variables, restart to change

7.3.1.open_ended_text: Solo developer handles everything. GitHub issues for tracking. No SLA/response times. Open source, self-service. Updates as npm versions.
7.3.1.multi_choice_text: Firefighting — fix issues as they arise, no scheduled maintenance

7.3.2.open_ended_text: Actively maintained by original author. Semantic versioning. Breaking changes require major bump. Framework format versioned separately. Stable tool with feature additions.
7.3.2.multi_choice_text: Build-and-run — the same team owns development and operations
